title: Gather the elders, convert many, and organize under the law
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, in the latter part of February 1831. It is addressed to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon. A letter Joseph wrote to Martin Harris on 22 February seems to allude to it, so it likely came before that date. The Church later set a conference for early June 1831, which Joseph’s history links to this call.
summary: The revelation says the elders should be called together from every direction, by letter or other means. If they are faithful, the Spirit will be poured out when they assemble. They will then preach repentance in the nearby regions. Many will be converted, giving the Saints power to organize under the laws of man. That organization will protect them from enemies and help them keep God’s laws. Finally the elders must visit the poor and needy and relieve them until all is done by the law.

contextNote.title: Why organize by the laws of man
contextNote.text: The young Church in Ohio held property and cared for the poor, and verse 5 says it had enemies. Verse 4 links growth to a practical step: enough converts would let the Saints organize “according to the laws of man”. Verse 5 gives the reasons. Such organization would keep enemies from having power over them and help them keep God’s laws. Verse 6 sets a duty beside it: relief of “the poor and the needy”. In this passage, organizing under the laws of man means using civil forms to protect the Church’s work, not replacing God’s law.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 41–44 presents these revelations as the Lord’s law to govern his Church. Verse 2 ties the outpouring of the Spirit to the elders gathering in faith; what does verse 6 add about what that gathering is for?
reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, latter part of February 1831, to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon, leading to a June 1831 conference. JSP notes the 22 February letter to Martin Harris suggests an earlier date, and weighs a 9 April elders’ meeting against the June conference, favoring June. Exact day unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote no longer claims verse 6 states the purpose of the legal organization; the text joins the two only by sequence.
